svg.text: Qualifying formats in real racing, 1949 to 2026
Each row is one qualifying format a series used. Each square is a real season. Grey rail: the series ran that year. Colour: the format.
Green formats work in Team Principal today. The others need a wishlist item (A1, A2, A5, A6, C8) or a new one.

Tag: what the game needs. In the game = works today. A1 to C8 = item in docs/DEVELOPER_WISHLIST.md. New = no item yet.
One session, best lap sets the grid.
Three timed parts. The slowest cars drop out after each part, the last part sets the front.
Oval runs, one car at a time
Each car runs alone for a few laps. The laps are averaged or the best one counts.
A short race sets the main race grid, or the places behind the direct qualifiers.
Two or more sessions, often on two days. The best lap from any of them sets the grid.
Groups, then a final for the fastest
The field is split into groups, or the fastest move on to a final session that sets the front of the grid.
Race 2 or race 3 starts in the finishing order of the race before, sometimes with the top places reversed.
The fastest cars run one flying lap each, alone on track, in a set order.
Like the F1 knockout, but with two or four parts, or with cars moving up from practice.
Each race of the weekend gets its own qualifying session.
Times of several drivers added up
Each driver of a car sets a time. The times are added or averaged.
Grid by points or a formula
Places are given by owner points, a performance formula or engine size, with no timed lap.
After the groups, the top eight go against the clock two at a time: quarter-finals, semi-finals, final.

Source: Team Principal modding rules coverage db (docs/history), qualifying columns. WRC, Dakar, Rallycross and Race of Champions left out. A season can use two formats, for example one for race 1 and a grid from race 1 for race 2. Grey only: no format researched yet.
